newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: No reason to doubt hardness of euro - Duisenberg.
newsitem.headline: No reason to doubt hardness of euro - Duisenberg.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said on Tuesday there was no reason to doubt that the euro would be a hard currency.

In a preface to the bank's 1996 annual report, Duisenberg wrote that Europe's single currency would be launched by a group of countries which had already succeeded in achieving low inflation, interest rates and budget deficits.

Furthermore, countries taking part in economic and monetary union (EMU) had agreed to entrust management of the single currency to an independent European Central Bank (ECB) committed to maintaining internal price stability or low inflation.
"Considering all this, doubts about the internal hardness of the euro would seem unfounded," he said.

Duisenberg said inflation in Europe was somewhat lower than in the United States, adding that the ECB's pursuit of low inflation in the euro zone would contribute to exchange rate stability against the U.S. dollar and other currencies.
However, in the event of a clash between the the internal and external stability of the euro, the former would prevail.

"And, in such a situation, in which inflation would thus be lower in Europe than in the United States and remain lower for a considerable period of time, concern should focus on the softness of the dollar rather than on the hardness of the euro," Duisenberg said.
